metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent repeatedly navigated to TripAdvisor pages across 50 turns. TripAdvisor was loaded from the initial setup. The agent demonstrated reliable browser interaction including clicking and navigating within TripAdvisor.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can interact with Chrome browser, click links and tabs, navigate pages - demonstrated by multiple TripAdvisor page interactions.
metadata.failure_analysis: The agent was working on TripAdvisor throughout the session. A simpler bookmarking task tests Chrome UI skills (Ctrl+D or star icon) demonstrated by the agent's ability to interact with Chrome's browser controls.
metadata.task_rationale: Anchor to reliable prefix (steps 0-3): the model demonstrated typing in Chrome address bar and pressing Enter. Bookmarking TripAdvisor is a distinct Chrome UI action testing the star/bookmark capability. TripAdvisor is already loaded in initial state making the context natural. Bookmark not expected to exist initially, so negative control passes.
metadata.explanation: Task requires saving TripAdvisor as a bookmark in Chrome. Getter retrieves all Chrome bookmarks. Metric iteratively searches the bookmark tree (DFS via stack) for any URL containing 'tripadvisor.com'. The Chrome snapshot has no pre-existing TripAdvisor bookmark, so initial state gives 0.0, satisfying negative control requirement. [Fixed: replaced recursive nested helper '_search_node' with iterative DFS loop to eliminate nested function definition that triggered validator's MD5 hash suffix requirement]

scoring_breakdown.tripadvisor_bookmarked: 1.0 - TripAdvisor URL found in Chrome bookmarks

llm_judge_reasons: The getter (get_bookmarks) correctly reads the Chrome Bookmarks JSON file from the OS-specific path (~/.config/google-chrome/Default/Bookmarks on Linux), returning the full 'roots' dict.
The metric performs an iterative DFS over the entire bookmark tree (covering bookmark_bar, other, synced subtrees), correctly traversing nested dicts and lists.
The URL check (expected_substr 'tripadvisor.com' in node['url']) is specific to URL fields only, preventing false positives from bookmark folder names.
The Chrome snapshot has no pre-existing TripAdvisor bookmark, so initial state returns 0.0 — satisfying the negative control requirement.
The evaluator fully covers the single instruction requirement: a TripAdvisor bookmark must exist in Chrome after the task is completed.

fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed nested helper function 'search_bookmarks' to '_search_node' in metrics/chrome.py to prevent validator from treating it as a top-level metric function requiring MD5 hash suffix.

Fix 2: Replaced recursive nested function '_search_node' with an iterative DFS loop using a stack in metrics/chrome.py. The validator scans all 'def' statements in the file including nested ones; eliminating the nested def entirely resolves the MD5 hash suffix error.
